newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SWEDISH BOND YIELDS HIGHER, CROWN LITTLE CHANGED.
newsitem.headline: SWEDISH BOND YIELDS HIGHER, CROWN LITTLE CHANGED.

text.p: Long Swedish bond yields were slightly higher around midday on Monday, hurt by U.S. markets but supported by a firmer German market, while the crown was little changed against the mark.
Long bond yields came off initial highs and dealers expected the yield curve to start flattening.
"I think the curve should start flattening around these levels," one dealer said when the spread between the 10-year and the three-year bond yield was 130 basis points.
Players focus on Bundesbank's Tuesday announcement and some speculate about a change-over to variable rates.
The six-month T-bill rate was flat at 4.31 percent while the 10-year bond yield rose two to 6.58 percent.
The crown was little changed at 4.2895 to the mark compared with 4.2820 late on Friday and dealers said trade was quiet after last week's turmoil.
"Most currencies showed large movements last week and now we see some profit-taking. People are for example buying back dollars for crowns," one dealer said.
He expected the crown to trade between 4.2800 and 4.3050 against the mark.
